o: ¡Oh perpetuo descubridor de los antípodas, hacha del mundo, ojo del cielo, meneo dulce de las cantimploras, Timbrio aquí, Febo allí, tirador acá, médico acullá, padre de la Poesía, inventor de la Música: tú que siempre sales, y, aunque lo parece, nunca te pones!
t: Oh perpetual discoverer of the antipodes, axe of the world, eye of the sky, sweet waggling of the tankards, Timbrius here, Phoebus there, archer yonder, physician here, father of Poetry, inventor of Music: you who always rise and, though it seems so, never set!

o: A ti digo, ¡oh sol, con cuya ayuda el hombre engendra al hombre!; a ti digo que me favorezcas, y alumbres la escuridad de mi ingenio, para que pueda discurrir por sus puntos en la narración del gobierno del gran Sancho Panza; que sin ti, yo me siento tibio, desmazalado y confuso.
t: To you I speak, O Sun, with whose help man engenders man! To you I speak, that you favor me and light the darkness of my wit, so that I may reason soundly in the narration of the government of the great Sancho Panza; for without you I feel tepid, listless, and confused.

o: Digo, pues, que con todo su acompañamiento llegó Sancho a un lugar de hasta mil vecinos, que era de los mejores que el duque tenía.
t: I say, then, that with all his retinue Sancho arrived at a place of up to a thousand inhabitants, one of the best the duke had.

o: Diéronle a entender que se llamaba la ínsula Barataria, o ya porque el lugar se llamaba Baratario, o ya por el barato con que se le había dado el gobierno.
t: They let him understand that it was called the insula Barataria, either because the place was called Baratario, or because of the cheapness with which the government had been handed over to him.

o: El traje, las barbas, la gordura y pequeñez del nuevo gobernador tenía admirada a toda la gente que el busilis del cuento no sabía, y aun a todos los que lo sabían, que eran muchos.
t: The dress, the beards, the fatness and smallness of the new governor had filled with wonder all the people who were not privy to the point of the story, and even all those who were, and they were many.

o: Finalmente, en sacándole de la iglesia, le llevaron a la silla del juzgado y le sentaron en ella; y el mayordomo del duque le dijo.
t: Finally, taking him out of the church, they carried him to the judge's chair and seated him in it; and the duke's steward said to him.

o: — Es costumbre antigua en esta ínsula, señor gobernador, que el que viene a tomar posesión desta famosa ínsula está obligado a responder a una pregunta que se le hiciere, que sea algo intricada y dificultosa, de cuya respuesta el pueblo toma y toca el pulso del ingenio de su nuevo gobernador; y así, o se alegra o se entristece con su venida.
t: — It is an ancient custom in this insula, sir governor, that whoever comes to take possession of this famous insula is obliged to answer a question that shall be put to him, something intricate and difficult, from whose answer the people gauge and take the measure of the wit of their new governor; and so they either rejoice or become sad at his coming.

o: En tanto que el mayordomo decía esto a Sancho, estaba él mirando unas grandes y muchas letras que en la pared frontera de su silla estaban escritas; y, como él no sabía leer, preguntó que qué eran aquellas pinturas que en aquella pared estaban. Fuele respondido.
t: While the steward was saying this to Sancho, he was looking at some large and many letters that were written on the wall opposite his chair; and, since he did not know how to read, he asked what those paintings on that wall were. He was answered.

o: — Señor, allí esta escrito y notado el día en que Vuestra Señoría tomó posesión desta ínsula, y dice el epitafio: Hoy día, a tantos de tal mes y de tal año, tomó la posesión desta ínsula el señor don Sancho Panza, que muchos años la goce.
t: — Sir, there it is written and noted the day on which Your Lordship took possession of this insula, and the epitaph reads: On this day, so many of such a month and such a year, Sir Don Sancho Panza took possession of this insula, may he enjoy it for many years.

o: — Y ¿a quién llaman don Sancho Panza? —preguntó Sancho.
t: — And whom do they call Don Sancho Panza? —asked Sancho.

o: — A vuestra señoría —respondió el mayordomo—, que en esta ínsula no ha entrado otro Panza sino el que está sentado en esa silla.
t: — Your Lordship —replied the steward—, for no other Panza has entered this insula than the one seated in that chair.

o: Pase adelante con su pregunta el señor mayordomo, que yo responderé lo mejor que supiere, ora se entristezca o no se entristezca el pueblo.
t: Let the lord steward proceed with his question, and I will answer as best I can, whether the people be saddened or not.

o: A este instante entraron en el juzgado dos hombres, el uno vestido de labrador y el otro de sastre, porque traía unas tijeras en la mano, y el sastre dijo.
t: At that moment two men entered the courtroom, one dressed as a laborer and the other as a tailor, for he carried a pair of shears in his hand, and the tailor said.

o: — ¿Es todo esto así, hermano? —preguntó Sancho.
t: — Is it all like this, brother? —asked Sancho.

o: — Sí, señor —respondió el hombre—, pero hágale vuestra merced que muestre las cinco caperuzas que me ha hecho.
t: — Yes, sir —replied the man—, but let your grace have him show the five hoods he has made for me.

o: — De buena gana —respondió el sastre.
t: — With great pleasure —replied the tailor.

o: Y, sacando encontinente la mano debajo del herreruelo, mostró en ella cinco caperuzas puestas en las cinco cabezas de los dedos de la mano, y dijo.
t: And, immediately pulling his hand from beneath his cloak, he showed five hoods worn on the five fingers of his hand, and said.

o: — He aquí las cinco caperuzas que este buen hombre me pide, y en Dios y en mi conciencia que no me ha quedado nada del paño, y yo daré la obra a vista de veedores del oficio.
t: — Here are the five hoods this good man asks of me, and on my soul and conscience, none of the cloth is left, and I will deliver the work before witnesses of the trade.

o: Todos los presentes se rieron de la multitud de las caperuzas y del nuevo pleito.
t: All those present laughed at the multitude of hoods and at the new suit.

o: Sancho se puso a considerar un poco, y dijo.
t: Sancho began to consider a little, and said.

o: — Paréceme que en este pleito no ha de haber largas dilaciones, sino juzgar luego a juicio de buen varón; y así, yo doy por sentencia que el sastre pierda las hechuras, y el labrador el paño, y las caperuzas se lleven a los presos de la cárcel, y no haya más.
t: — It seems to me there should be no long delays in this case, but that it be judged at once, by sound common sense; and so I give as sentence that the tailor lose the labor and the farmer the cloth, and that the hoods be taken to the prisoners in the jail, and that there be no more about it.

o: Si la sentencia pasada de la bolsa del ganadero movió a admiración a los circunstantes, ésta les provocó a risa; pero, en fin, se hizo lo que mandó el gobernador; ante el cual se presentaron dos hombres ancianos; el uno traía una cañaheja por báculo, y el sin báculo dijo.
t: If the sentence handed down over the herdsman's purse moved the bystanders to wonder, this one provoked them to laughter; but in the end, what the governor commanded was done; and before him two old men presented themselves; one carried a leather strap for a staff, and the one without a staff said:

o: Yo no tengo testigos ni del prestado ni de la vuelta, porque no me los ha vuelto; querría que vuestra merced le tomase juramento, y si jurare que me los ha vuelto, yo se los perdono para aquí y para delante de Dios.
t: I have no witnesses, neither of the loan nor of the return, because he has not returned them to me; I would like your grace to have him swear, and if he swears that he has returned them to me, I forgive him them, here and before God.

o: — ¿Qué decís vos a esto, buen viejo del báculo? —dijo Sancho.
t: — What do you say to this, good old man with the staff? — said Sancho.

o: A lo que dijo el viejo.
t: To what the old man said.

o: — Yo, señor, confieso que me los prestó, y baje vuestra merced esa vara; y, pues él lo deja en mi juramento, yo juraré como se los he vuelto y pagado real y verdaderamente.
t: — Yes, sir, I confess that he lent them to me; and let your grace lower that rod; and since he leaves it to my oath, I will swear that I have returned and paid them truly and in full.

o: Viendo lo cual el gran gobernador, preguntó al acreedor qué respondía a lo que decía su contrario; y dijo que sin duda alguna su deudor debía de decir verdad, porque le tenía por hombre de bien y buen cristiano, y que a él se le debía de haber olvidado el cómo y cuándo se los había vuelto, y que desde allí en adelante jamás le pidiría nada.
t: Which the great governor seeing, asked the creditor what he answered to what his opponent said; and he replied that without any doubt his debtor must be telling the truth, because he held him for an honest man and a good Christian, and that he himself must have forgotten how and when he had returned them, and that from that day forward he would never ask him for anything more.

o: Tornó a tomar su báculo el deudor, y, bajando la cabeza, se salió del juzgado.
t: The debtor took up his staff again, and, bowing his head, left the courtroom.

o: Visto lo cual Sancho, y que sin más ni más se iba, y viendo también la paciencia del demandante, inclinó la cabeza sobre el pecho, y, poniéndose el índice de la mano derecha sobre las cejas y las narices, estuvo como pensativo un pequeño espacio, y luego alzó la cabeza y mandó que le llamasen al viejo del báculo, que ya se había ido.
t: Which Sancho seeing, and that he was leaving just as he was, and seeing also the patience of the plaintiff, inclined his head over his chest, and, placing the index finger of his right hand upon his brows and nose, remained thoughtful for a little while, and then raised his head and ordered that the old man with the staff be called, though he had already gone.

o: Trujéronsele, y, en viéndole Sancho, le dijo.
t: They brought him, and Sancho, upon seeing him, said:

o: — Dadme, buen hombre, ese báculo, que le he menester.
t: — Give me, good man, that staff, for I have need of it.

o: — De muy buena gana —respondió el viejo—: hele aquí, señor.
t: — With great pleasure —answered the old man—: here it is, sir.

o: Y púsosele en la mano.
t: And he put it in his hand.

o: Tomóle Sancho, y, dándosele al otro viejo, le dijo.
t: Sancho took it, and, handing it to the other old man, said:

o: — Andad con Dios, que ya vais pagado.
t: — Go with God, for you are paid now.

o: —respondió el viejo—.
t: — answered the old man—.

o: Pues, ¿vale esta cañaheja diez escudos de oro?
t: Now, is this leather staff worth ten gold escudos?

o: — Sí —dijo el gobernador—; o si no, yo soy el mayor porro del mundo.
t: — Yes —said the governor—; or else I am the greatest fool in the world.

o: Y ahora se verá si tengo yo caletre para gobernar todo un reino.
t: And now it will be seen whether I have any wit for governing a whole kingdom.

o: Y mandó que allí, delante de todos, se rompiese y abriese la caña.
t: And he ordered that there, before everyone, the cane be broken and opened.

o: Hízose así, y en el corazón della hallaron diez escudos en oro.
t: So it was done, and in the midst of it they found ten gold shields.

o: Quedaron todos admirados, y tuvieron a su gobernador por un nuevo Salomón.
t: Everyone was amazed, and they held their governor to be a new Solomon.

o: De donde se podía colegir que los que gobiernan, aunque sean unos tontos, tal vez los encamina Dios en sus juicios; y más, que él había oído contar otro caso como aquél al cura de su lugar, y que él tenía tan gran memoria, que, a no olvidársele todo aquello de que quería acordarse, no hubiera tal memoria en toda la ínsula.
t: From which it could be gathered that those who govern, even if they are fools, are perhaps guided by God in His judgments; and moreover, he had heard the priest of his place tell of another case like that one, and that he had such a great memory that, if he did not forget everything he wanted to remember, there was no such memory in all the island.

o: Finalmente, el un viejo corrido y el otro pagado, se fueron, y los presentes quedaron admirados, y el que escribía las palabras, hechos y movimientos de Sancho no acababa de determinarse si le tendría y pondría por tonto o por discreto.
t: Finally, the one old man shamed and the other paid, they went away, and those present were amazed, and the one who wrote down the words, deeds, and movements of Sancho could not make up his mind whether to hold him and set him down as a fool or as a wise man.

o: Luego, acabado este pleito, entró en el juzgado una mujer asida fuertemente de un hombre vestido de ganadero rico, la cual venía dando grandes voces, diciendo.
t: Then, that dispute being over, a woman entered the courtroom clinging tightly to a man dressed as a rich cattle dealer, and she came crying out loudly, saying:

o: — ¡Justicia, señor gobernador, justicia, y si no la hallo en la tierra, la iré a buscar al cielo!
t: "Justice, sir governor, justice! And if I do not find it on earth, I will go and seek it in heaven!"

o: — Aun eso está por averiguar: si tiene limpias o no las manos este galán — dijo Sancho.
t: "That is still to be seen: whether this young man has clean hands or not," said Sancho.

o: Y, volviéndose al hombre, le dijo qué decía y respondía a la querella de aquella mujer.
t: And, turning to the man, he told him what the woman said and answered in reply to her complaint.

o: El cual, todo turbado, respondió.
t: Who, all confused, replied:

o: Dice que la forcé, y miente, para el juramento que hago o pienso hacer; y ésta es toda la verdad, sin faltar meaja.
t: "She says I forced her, and she lies, by the oath I make or mean to make; and this is the whole truth, not a grain of it missing."

o: Entonces el gobernador le preguntó si traía consigo algún dinero en plata; él dijo que hasta veinte ducados tenía en el seno, en una bolsa de cuero.
t: Then the governor asked him whether he had any money in silver about him; he said he had as much as twenty ducats in his bosom, in a leather purse.

o: Apenas salió, cuando Sancho dijo al ganadero, que ya se le saltaban las lágrimas, y los ojos y el corazón se iban tras su bolsa.
t: As soon as he had gone out, Sancho said to the cattle dealer, whose tears were already welling up, that his eyes and his heart were after his purse.

o: — Buen hombre, id tras aquella mujer y quitadle la bolsa, aunque no quiera, y volved aquí con ella.
t: "Good man, go after that woman and take the purse from her, whether she wants it or not, and come back here with it."

o: Y no lo dijo a tonto ni a sordo, porque luego partió como un rayo y fue a lo que se le mandaba.
t: And he said it neither idly nor in vain, for he set off like a bolt of lightning and did as he was told.

o: Todos los presentes estaban suspensos, esperando el fin de aquel pleito, y de allí a poco volvieron el hombre y la mujer más asidos y aferrados que la vez primera: ella la saya levantada y en el regazo puesta la bolsa, y el hombre pugnando por quitársela; mas no era posible, según la mujer la defendía, la cual daba voces diciendo.
t: All those present were left in suspense, waiting for the outcome of that lawsuit, and shortly thereafter the man and the woman came back more tightly clasped and fastened than the first time: she with hers raised and the purse laid in her lap, and the man struggling to take it from her; but it was not possible, since the woman defended it, and she was crying out, saying:

o: — ¡Justicia de Dios y del mundo!
t: "Justice of God and of the world!"

o: Mire vuestra merced, señor gobernador, la poca vergüenza y el poco temor deste desalmado, que, en mitad de poblado y en mitad de la calle, me ha querido quitar la bolsa que vuestra merced mandó darme.
t: "Look, your worship, sir governor, at the shamelessness and the lack of fear of this villain, who, in the middle of the town and in the middle of the street, has tried to take from me the purse your worship ordered to be given to me."

o: — Y ¿háosla quitado?
t: "And has he taken it from you?"

o: —preguntó el gobernador.
t: "asked the governor."

o: —respondió la mujer—.
t: "replied the woman."

o: Antes me dejara yo quitar la vida que me quiten la bolsa.
t: I'd sooner let them take my life than have them take the bag from me.

o: ¡Bonita es la niña!
t: What a pretty girl!

o: ¡Otros gatos me han de echar a las barbas, que no este desventurado y asqueroso!
t: Let other cats be the ones to mock me, and not this wretched and filthy one!

o: ¡Tenazas y martillos, mazos y escoplos no serán bastantes a sacármela de las uñas, ni aun garras de leones: antes el ánima de en mitad en mitad de las carnes!
t: Pincers and hammers, mallets and chisels will not be enough to pull it out of my claws, nor even lions' claws: I would sooner give up my soul in the very midst of my flesh!

o: — Ella tiene razón —dijo el hombre—, y yo me doy por rendido y sin fuerzas, y confieso que las mías no son bastantes para quitársela, y déjola.
t: "She is right," said the man, "and I yield myself conquered and without strength. I confess that mine are not enough to take it from her, so let her keep it."

o: Entonces el gobernador dijo a la mujer.
t: Then the governor said to the woman.

o: — Mostrad, honrada y valiente, esa bolsa.
t: "Show me, honorable and valiant woman, that bag."

o: Ella se la dio luego, y el gobernador se la volvió al hombre, y dijo a la esforzada y no forzada.
t: She handed it to him at once, and the governor gave it back to the man, and said to the stout-hearted and unforced woman.

o: — Hermana mía, si el mismo aliento y valor que habéis mostrado para defender esta bolsa le mostrárades, y aun la mitad menos, para defender vuestro cuerpo, las fuerzas de Hércules no os hicieran fuerza.
t: "My sister, if you had shown the same spirit and courage in defending your body that you have shown in defending this bag—or even half of it—the strength of Hercules would not have prevailed against you.

o: Andad con Dios, y mucho de enhoramala, y no paréis en toda esta ínsula ni en seis leguas a la redonda, so pena de docientos azotes.
t: Go with God, and much good may it do you; and do not stop anywhere on this whole island, nor within six leagues around it, on pain of two hundred lashes.

o: ¡Andad luego digo, churrillera, desvergonzada y embaidora!
t: Off with you, I say, saucy, shameless, and deceitful wench!

o: Espantóse la mujer y fuese cabizbaja y mal contenta, y el gobernador dijo al hombre.
t: The woman was frightened and went off with her head bowed, ill content, and the governor said to the man.

o: — Buen hombre, andad con Dios a vuestro lugar con vuestro dinero, y de aquí adelante, si no le queréis perder, procurad que no os venga en voluntad de yogar con nadie.
t: "Good man, go with God to your place with your money, and from now on, if you don't want to lose it, take care that you never feel like playing with anyone."

o: El hombre le dio las gracias lo peor que supo, y fuese, y los circunstantes quedaron admirados de nuevo de los juicios y sentencias de su nuevo gobernador.
t: The man thanked him as best he knew how and went away, and the bystanders were again filled with wonder at the judgments and sentences of their new governor.

o: Todo lo cual, notado de su coronista, fue luego escrito al duque, que con gran deseo lo estaba esperando.
t: All of which, noted by his chronicler, was soon written to the duke, who had been awaiting it with great longing.

o: Y quédese aquí el buen Sancho, que es mucha la priesa que nos da su amo, alborozado con la música de Altisidora.
t: And let good Sancho stay here, for his master gives us great haste, all in a flutter over the music of Altisidora.

o: Del temeroso espanto cencerril y gatuno que recibió don Quijote en el discurso de los amores de la enamorada Altisidora.
t: Of the dreadful braying and mewing fright that Don Quixote received in the course of the loves of the enamored Altisidora.

o: Dejamos al gran don Quijote envuelto en los pensamientos que le habían causado la música de la enamorada doncella Altisidora.
t: We leave the great Don Quixote wrapped in the thoughts that the music of the enamored maiden Altisidora had caused him.

o: Acostóse con ellos, y, como si fueran pulgas, no le dejaron dormir ni sosegar un punto, y juntábansele los que le faltaban de sus medias; pero, como es ligero el tiempo, y no hay barranco que le detenga, corrió caballero en las horas, y con mucha presteza llegó la de la mañana.
t: He lay down with them, and, as if they were fleas, they would not let him sleep or rest for a moment, and they swarmed over him, the ones that were missing from his stockings; but, since time is swift and no ravine can hold it back, it ran swiftly through the hours, and morning came very speedily.

o: Don Quijote, que lo vio, llegándose a ellas, dijo.
t: Don Quixote, who saw it, as he drew near to them, said.

o: — Ya sé yo de qué proceden estos accidentes.
t: — I know well enough what causes these accidents.

o: — No sé yo de qué —respondió la amiga—, porque Altisidora es la doncella más sana de toda esta casa, y yo nunca la he sentido un ¡ay! en cuanto ha que la conozco, que mal hayan cuantos caballeros andantes hay en el mundo, si es que todos son desagradecidos.
t: — I don't know —answered the friend—, because Altisidora is the healthiest maiden in the whole house, and I have never heard her say an 'ouch' since I came to know her. Heaven take its toll on all the knight-errants in the world, if indeed they are all ungrateful.

o: Váyase vuesa merced, señor don Quijote, que no volverá en sí esta pobre niña en tanto que vuesa merced aquí estuviere.
t: Let your grace depart, sir Don Quixote, for this poor girl will not come to her senses as long as your grace is here.

o: A lo que respondió don Quijote.
t: To which Don Quixote replied.

o: — Haga vuesa merced, señora, que se me ponga un laúd esta noche en mi aposento, que yo consolaré lo mejor que pudiere a esta lastimada doncella; que en los principios amorosos los desengaños prestos suelen ser remedios calificados.
t: — Let your grace have a lute brought to my chamber tonight, madam, and I shall comfort this wounded maiden as best I can; for in the early stages of love, ready disappointments are usually proven remedies.

o: Y con esto se fue, porque no fuese notado de los que allí le viesen.
t: And with this he went away, so that he might not be noticed by those who saw him there.

o: No se hubo bien apartado, cuando, volviendo en sí la desmayada Altisidora, dijo a su compañera.
t: He had not long withdrawn when Altisidora, coming to her senses, said to her companion.

o: — Menester será que se le ponga el laúd, que sin duda don Quijote quiere darnos música, y no será mala, siendo suya.
t: — We must have the lute brought, for without a doubt Don Quixote means to give us music, and it will not be bad, coming from him.

o: Y la duquesa aquel día real y verdaderamente despachó a un paje suyo, que había hecho en la selva la figura encantada de Dulcinea, a Teresa Panza, con la carta de su marido Sancho Panza, y con el lío de ropa que había dejado para que se le enviase, encargándole le trujese buena relación de todo lo que con ella pasase.
t: And that day the duchess truly and properly dispatched one of her pages, who had made in the forest the enchanted figure of Dulcinea, to Teresa Panza, with her husband Sancho Panza's letter and with the bundle of clothes he had left to be sent to her, charging him to bring a good account of everything that had happened to her.

o: -Suelen las fuerzas de amor sacar de quicio a las almas, tomando por instrumento la ociosidad descuidada.
t: — The forces of love are wont to drive souls out of their wits, taking careless idleness as their instrument.

o: Suele el coser y el labrar, y el estar siempre ocupada, ser antídoto al veneno de las amorosas ansias.
t: Sewing and working, and always being busy, are usually an antidote to the poison of amorous anxieties.

o: Las doncellas recogidas que aspiran a ser casadas, la honestidad es la dote y voz de sus alabanzas.
t: For maidens who are kept at home and aspire to be married, honesty is their dowry and the voice of their praise.

o: Los andantes caballeros, y los que en la corte andan, requiébranse con las libres, con las honestas se casan.
t: Knight-errants, and those who move about at court, dally with the free ones; with the honest ones they marry.

o: Hay amores de levante, que entre huéspedes se tratan, que llegan presto al poniente, porque en el partirse acaban.
t: There are loves of the passing kind, which are treated among guests and come quickly to their end, because they end with the parting.

o: El amor recién venido, que hoy llegó y se va mañana, las imágines no deja bien impresas en el alma.
t: Love newly come, which arrives today and leaves tomorrow, leaves no images well impressed on the soul.

o: Pintura sobre pintura ni se muestra ni señala; y do hay primera belleza, la segunda no hace baza.
t: Paint upon paint is neither shown nor pointed out; and where there is a first beauty, the second does not make a gain.

o: Dulcinea del Toboso del alma en la tabla rasa tengo pintada de modo que es imposible borrarla.
t: Dulcinea del Toboso I have painted on the blank tablet of my soul in such a way that it is impossible to erase her.

o: La firmeza en los amantes es la parte más preciada, por quien hace amor milagros, y asimesmo los levanta.
t: Steadfastness in lovers is the most precious part, for it makes love perform miracles, and likewise raises them.

o: Fue tan grande el ruido de los cencerros y el mayar de los gatos, que, aunque los duques habían sido inventores de la burla, todavía les sobresaltó; y, temeroso, don Quijote quedó pasmado.
t: The noise of the bells and the caterwauling of the cats was so great that, although the dukes had been the inventors of the prank, it startled them nonetheless; and, fearful, Don Quixote was left astounded.

o: Y quiso la suerte que dos o tres gatos se entraron por la reja de su estancia, y, dando de una parte a otra, parecía que una región de diablos andaba en ella.
t: And fortune willed it that two or three cats got in through the grating of his chamber, and, going from one side to the other, it seemed as if a whole region of devils were moving about in it.

o: Apagaron las velas que en el aposento ardían, y andaban buscando por do escaparse.
t: They put out the candles that were burning in the chamber, and went about seeking in every way to escape.

o: El descolgar y subir del cordel de los grandes cencerros no cesaba; la mayor parte de la gente del castillo, que no sabía la verdad del caso, estaba suspensa y admirada.
t: The unhooking and hoisting of the great clappers never ceased; most of the people in the castle, who did not know the truth of the matter, stood suspended in wonder and admiration.

o: Levantóse don Quijote en pie, y, poniendo mano a la espada, comenzó a tirar estocadas por la reja y a decir a grandes voces.
t: Don Quixote rose to his feet and, laying hand on his sword, began to thrust at the grille and to shout at the top of his voice.

o: — ¡Afuera, malignos encantadores!
t: "Out, you wicked enchanters!"

o: ¡Afuera, canalla hechiceresca, que yo soy don Quijote de la Mancha, contra quien no valen ni tienen fuerza vuestras malas intenciones!
t: Out, you sorcerous rabble, for I am Don Quixote of La Mancha, against whom your evil intentions are worthless and powerless!

o: Y, volviéndose a los gatos que andaban por el aposento, les tiró muchas cuchilladas; ellos acudieron a la reja, y por allí se salieron, aunque uno, viéndose tan acosado de las cuchilladas de don Quijote, le saltó al rostro y le asió de las narices con las uñas y los dientes, por cuyo dolor don Quijote comenzó a dar los mayores gritos que pudo.
t: And, turning to the cats that were prowling about the room, he dealt them many slashes; they rushed to the grille and escaped that way, though one of them, seeing itself so hard pressed by Don Quixote's slashes, sprang at his face and seized him by the nose with claws and teeth, at which pain Don Quixote began to give the loudest cries he could.

o: Oyendo lo cual el duque y la duquesa, y considerando lo que podía ser, con mucha presteza acudieron a su estancia, y, abriendo con llave maestra, vieron al pobre caballero pugnando con todas sus fuerzas por arrancar el gato de su rostro.
t: Hearing which, the duke and duchess, considering what it might be, hastened to his chamber with all speed and, opening the door with a master key, saw the poor knight struggling with all his might to pull the cat off his face.

o: Entraron con luces y vieron la desigual pelea; acudió el duque a despartirla, y don Quijote dijo a voces.
t: They entered with lights and saw the unequal fight; the duke came up to break it off, and Don Quixote cried out loudly.

o: — ¡No me le quite nadie!
t: "Let no one take him from me!"

o: ¡Déjenme mano a mano con este demonio, con este hechicero, con este encantador, que yo le daré a entender de mí a él quién es don Quijote de la Mancha!
t: Let me deal hand to hand with this demon, this sorcerer, this enchanter, and I will make him understand from me who Don Quixote of La Mancha is!

o: Pero el gato, no curándose destas amenazas, gruñía y apretaba.
t: But the cat, heedless of these threats, growled and tightened its grip.

o: Mas, en fin, el duque se le desarraigó y le echó por la reja.
t: In the end, however, the duke uprooted it and threw it out through the grille.

o: Quedó don Quijote acribado el rostro y no muy sanas las narices, aunque muy despechado porque no le habían dejado fenecer la batalla que tan trabada tenía con aquel malandrín encantador.
t: Don Quixote was left with his face riddled and his nose not in very good condition, though he was much more vexed because they had not let him finish the battle he had so tangled up with that rascally enchanter.

o: Hicieron traer aceite de Aparicio, y la misma Altisidora, con sus blanquísimas manos, le puso unas vendas por todo lo herido; y, al ponérselas, con voz baja le dijo.
t: They had oil of Aparicio brought, and Altisidora herself, with her snow-white hands, applied bandages to all his wounds; and as she put them on, she said to him in a low voice.

o: — Todas estas malandanzas te suceden, empedernido caballero, por el pecado de tu dureza y pertinacia; y plega a Dios que se le olvide a Sancho tu escudero el azotarse, porque nunca salga de su encanto esta tan amada tuya Dulcinea, ni tú lo goces, ni llegues a tálamo con ella, a lo menos viviendo yo, que te adoro.
t: "All these mishaps befall you, obdurate knight, for the sin of your harshness and obstinacy; and God grant that your squire Sancho forget to whip himself, and that your beloved Dulcinea never leave her enchantment, nor you enjoy her, nor reach the bridal chamber with her, at least while I live, who adore you."

o: A todo esto no respondió don Quijote otra palabra si no fue dar un profundo suspiro, y luego se tendió en su lecho, agradeciendo a los duques la merced, no porque él tenía temor de aquella canalla gatesca, encantadora y cencerruna, sino porque había conocido la buena intención con que habían venido a socorrerle.
t: To all this Don Quixote replied not a word except a deep sigh, and then he lay down on his bed, giving thanks to the duke and duchess for their favor, not because he feared that Ghibelline rabble, sorcerous and clanging, but because he had come to know the good intention with which they had come to his aid.
